areas.name: Sequencing / Over-the-top
areas.description: Starting the downswing with the lower body instead of the arms/shoulders. Over-the-top is treated as a symptom of this rather than a separate fault.

timeline.note: Coach cue: "let the arms drop" (feel cue for passive arms, not skipping the lower body). Recommended step-change-of-direction and pump-drill.
Swing-video review confirmed arms/shoulders start the downswing before the hips clear; suggested pump-drill and step-change-of-direction.

First range block on step-change-of-direction + pump-drill since the lesson. Block average (99yd carry, 106mph) is below baseline but steadier than it first looked from 3 individually-logged shots — expected while isolating the new movement. Numbers can't confirm the sequencing itself changed, that needs video.

User's own read on the following contact block: "little consistency at the start but felt like finding a good groove in the sequencing toward the end." Matches the numbers — launch/apex improved through the block at the same ball speed as the sequencing block. Worth checking at the next lesson whether this held up under transfer/pressure-test, or was specific to slow drill reps.

Driver transfer block: big, consistent right curve across all shots (avg 38.3yd offline right) — the textbook signature of an over-the-top/outside-in path, and it showed up hard once full speed and the driver came back into it. The iron drill work didn't transfer here yet. Worth naming specifically to Adrian next lesson.

Final pressure-test block: user felt they'd found "the right driver feel" but described it as more vertical than their iron swing — flagged as a concern, not confirmed as good, since a normal driver swing should feel shallower/flatter than irons, not steeper, and "more vertical" overlaps with what over-the-top looks like. Best distance of the day (193yd avg carry) but less consistent miss direction than the one-way-right transfer block. Genuinely good question for Adrian: driver hasn't been covered in a lesson yet.

Real video, driver, extra balls after the session: frame-by-frame confirms the arms/club drop from the top before the hips clear, same pattern as the 9/12 lesson's 7-iron video review — now confirmed on driver at full speed, not just irons or slow drills. Answers the pressure-test question directly: the "more vertical" feel was the fault, not a fix. Top-of-backswing position itself is solid; the issue is entirely the transition.

5-swing video filmed right after a specific in-the-moment cue (hip-first, 80% speed). Same arms-before-hips pattern held across all 3 swings that could be assessed — the cue didn't visibly change the sequencing in these reps. Not unusual for one cue over a handful of swings, but confirms this needs slow isolated driver-specific drill work (today's drills were 7-iron only) and live coaching, not more self-directed full-speed reps.

areas.name: Center-Face Contact
areas.description: Consistency of strike location across the face, independent of the sequencing fault.

timeline.note: First on-course evidence for this area: toe and topped strikes off the tee all round at Ramsdale (18-hole par 3, shot 105).

Warm-up wedge shot's low launch/apex looks like a thin or topped strike rather than a flush one, consistent with the toe/top pattern from Ramsdale. Today's session includes impact tape and coin-under-ball to get direct feedback instead of inferring from ball flight.

Impact tape + coin-under-ball block: launch angle and apex both improved versus the earlier sequencing-drill block at the same ball speed (12deg/38ft vs 8deg/21ft), pointing at cleaner contact rather than just a club change. First real positive signal for this area since the Ramsdale toe/top pattern showed up.

areas.name: Distance / Ball Speed Consistency
areas.description: How consistently the swing produces its top-end numbers rather than one-off flush hits. Baseline: ~150yd average 7-iron carry, ~170yd on a clean strike, up to 183yd carry / 213yd total on a flush hit (131 mph ball speed, 14 degree launch).

timeline.note: Flush 7-iron: 131 mph ball speed, 14 degree launch, 183yd carry / 213yd total. Well above the ~150yd average carry, showing the gap between best and average strikes.
First wedge numbers logged: 89.5 mph ball speed, 85.4yd carry, 117yd total on a 50-degree wedge. No prior wedge baseline to compare against.

Sequencing drill block average across 25 shots: 99yd carry, 106mph ball speed, 139yd total — below the ~150yd/131mph baseline but a steadier picture than the 3 individually-logged shots alone suggested (one of which was a 53.7yd offline outlier).

First 8i numbers: 25-shot average of 106mph ball speed, 117yd carry, 141yd total. Same ball speed as the earlier 7i block but higher carry/launch/apex despite less loft — cleaner contact as the session progressed, not just a different club.

First driver numbers: 25-ball transfer block average of 150mph ball speed but only 177yd carry, with a large consistent right curve (avg 38.3yd offline). High ball speed poorly converted to distance — heavy slice spin is the likely cause, not lack of power.

Pressure test block average: 154mph ball speed, 193yd carry — the best driver distance of the day, ahead of the transfer block. One visible shot (332yd carry, 117.3yd offline) looks like a likely mis-tracked/anomalous reading, not a real swing; kept logged but not weighted.
